sources_read: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row 48 (check 47), Internal Quality Checks row 48 (check 47), Deterministic Checks rows on check-dockerfiles.py and check-pip-pinning.sh
rules/projects/webdev-task-template (task.toml, tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/*, tests/.dockerignore, environment/Dockerfile; compared with diff)
task/instruction.md and task/environment/instructions/*.md (searched for clock/date rules)
task/solution/app/server.js, src/runtime.ts, src/app.tsx (time sources), solution/solve.sh, package.json
evidence: Judge agent and model: task/task.toml:30-35 holds the [verifier.env] block byte-equal to the frozen block in staged-task-contract.md (REWARDKIT_JUDGE = "claude-code", REWARDKIT_MODEL = "z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx", ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL = "https://openrouter.ai/api", ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}", ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""); diff of task.toml against the template shows only identity/metadata lines 5-7 and 10-15 differ. All five judge.toml files carry only `judge = "claude-code"` (line 2) with no model, temperature or reasoning setting. test.sh:63-66 exits with zero reward when REWARDKIT_JUDGE or REWARDKIT_MODEL is unset, so there is no silent fallback model. Pinned CLIs and browser: task/tests/Dockerfile:16-22 `@anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.281`, `@openai/codex@0.151.0`, `@playwright/mcp@0.0.79`, `express@5.1.0`, `better-sqlite3@12.4.1`; line 31 `harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7`; lines 33-38 install Chromium through the Playwright CLI bundled inside the pinned @playwright/mcp package and every judge.toml uses `--executable-path=/usr/local/bin/chromium`. Shared files: tests/Dockerfile, tests/test.sh, tests/scoring.toml, tests/tools/restart_mcp.py, tests/tools/score.py, tests/.dockerignore and environment/Dockerfile are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff -q silent). Fixed clock: no graded rule depends on the run date. The seed is `"snippets": []`, no criterion or brief line names a calendar date, age, 'today' or a displayed timestamp, and the golden's `new Date().toISOString()` values (server.js:71,84,111) are stored but never graded. The only time rules are relative durations (five-second run budget in behaviour.md:5, 'within about five seconds' cross-tab refresh in behaviour.md:11), graded with slack ('within about ten seconds', 'up to ten seconds', 'wait at least eight more seconds'), so they do not vary with the run date. Notes, not defects for this row: (a) base images use floating tags `node:22-bookworm-slim` and `python:3.12-slim` and apt packages are unversioned; both are template-controlled and the deterministic sheet treats unpinned apt as a NOTE. (b) Three functional criteria race the judge against a four-second timer (cw_output_before_failure_kept, cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, cw_newer_run_supersedes); the last two fail the app if the judge is twice too slow. That is real-time dependence on judge latency, not on the run date; in the hosted run on the earlier candidate the judge reported 'Stop was pressed 146ms after Run' and 'the newer Run started 286ms after the old one', so the race is feasible, but it is not measured on these bytes. No configured judge run exists for these bytes; the pinning facts above are source facts and do not need one. Raw evidence index: all 22 listed artifact SHA256 values recomputed and match.
